verdict: The bones are editorial and parts genuinely reach the signed standard: the 860-calorie numeral descends straight from benchmark beat 13, the label-left/serif-right hairline ledger is beat 19's grammar, the becoming cover's 48pt thesis sits at the question register, and the bubble-less typeset chat is nearly a printed correspondence page. But the frames still read engineered because chrome sits ON the typography instead of dissolving into it — a camera FAB disc, a hamburger, outlined chips, a bordered text field, a capsule tab bar with labels, and 12 progress dashes are all controls the benchmark never needed. Evening Home stacks five different grammars (headline, ledger, chips, kept line, form field) on one scroll, and on every page the whitespace is trailing leftover — content stops at 60% and nothing claims the rest — where the benchmark either centers the statement in the field (beat 19) or bounds the air with a single foot element (beat 10). One register of scale is missing almost everywhere: 40-44pt heroes against the onboarding's 52pt, and the masthead-as-cover-art move never happens.

compositions.composition: The day as a broadsheet front page, three stacked movements and nothing else. Top: the 13pt tracked date eyebrow alone (camera disc and hamburger deleted). Upper third: the kept sentence at 52pt across two lines, full-bleed hairline beneath it like a contract's signature line, the 36pt hollow ✦ seal seated on the rule at the right margin, the 17pt standfirst beneath. Center (the page's optical center): 96pt "860" + 30pt italic calories + one 20pt caption "room for ~600". Foot: three ledger rows — protein 62 of 90 / overnight fast, counts tomorrow / steps 6,420 — ending in a final full-bleed hairline that BOUNDS the remaining cream, so the air below is a composed field, not leftover. Tapping the kept sentence opens the camera; there is no other control on the page.

The close as a colophon page in exactly one grammar: a ledger she finishes writing. "closing the day." at 52pt, then four hairline rows — protein 62 of 90g / tomorrow, a balanced day / today felt ________ / best plate ________. The last two rows are content, not controls: tapping "today felt" sets proud · okay · tender as 34pt serif words full-bleed beneath the row, cross-off on tap (the onboarding gesture), the chosen word typesetting into the blank; tapping "best plate" drops a caret on the bare rule and her words become the row. Chips, the text-field capsule, and the duplicate "snap a meal" line are gone. The finished page is a completed typeset ledger — the screenshot of a day well closed.

An actual magazine cover, top-heavy masthead + full-bleed image. "becoming" as a 68pt italic masthead owning the top, "WEEK 2 OF 20 · FINDING STEADY" eyebrow beneath, the week's thesis staying at 52pt. The entire lower half — currently unclaimed cream — becomes one edge-to-edge editorial photograph: her best plate of the week, bottom-anchored, a cream scrim dissolving its top edge into the page (beat 13 already proves the full-bleed photo grammar; the brand owns this photography and shows none of it). The folio line sits ON the photo's foot in 13pt caps. Dashes deleted. "talk it through ↗" stays as the single italic action line under the thesis.

(Prescribed — the spread captures were byte-identical to the cover, so this is directive, not critique.) Every spread obeys one template so the book feels bound: eyebrow, ONE display element, one caption, folio. Weight spread: 96pt "74.2" + italic unit as the headline; the trend line drawn as a single hairline figure crossing the full page width at optical center, raw weigh-ins as small dots, no axes, no frame; one 20pt caption line; folio at the foot. Pacing spread: the mounds figure full-width with the morning→night baseline as the page's only rule, the 52pt claim above it, folio below. The repetition of the template page-to-page IS the printed-book feeling.

A correspondence page with one voice. jeni's prose stays 21pt cocoa as the body text of the page; her own messages drop to 17pt rose italic, right-indented as marginal notes, so the page reads as jeni's letter annotated by her rather than two equal columns. Hairline date rules between days. The input becomes the page's last line: a bare full-bleed hairline, ghost italic "talk to jeni" at 20pt, typed words setting in rose italic on the rule, "SEND" appearing as 13pt tracked caps at the rule's right end only once text exists. Capsule and circle button deleted; the ghost "today" artifact and the duplicated message pair cleaned before this frame is ever screenshot.

checklist_iconic.diagnosis: The kept line is currently one hairline row among visually equal rows — same width and near the same weight as the ledger rows below it — with a 22pt seal at 35% opacity floating off the right end like a disclosure chevron. Worse, the line is not even the interaction: the actual tap target is the camera disc parked in the header, so the signature is a label pointing at a control somewhere else. Nothing about one quiet row says "screenshot this"; it reads as the first row of a table.
checklist_iconic.proposal: ONE SENTENCE, ONE RULE, ONE SEAL — the day as a signature line, and the sentence IS the interface. The kept line sets at 52pt over two lines with a full-bleed hairline beneath (a contract's signing line) and the 36pt hollow ✦ seated on the rule at the right margin. Tap anywhere on the sentence → the camera opens (the header disc is deleted; control becomes content). On completion the seal fills rose with a soft haptic swell and an animated hairline strikes through the sentence — the onboarding's own cross-off gesture at hero scale — then tomorrow's line typesets beneath. Kept days accumulate DOWN the page as struck serif sentences each ending in a filled rose seal: a ledger of kept days in pure typography. That stack is the screenshot — it survives any crop, contains zero chrome, and nothing else on iOS looks like it. Buildable today: Text + animated-width rule overlay + the existing seal glyph + BreathHaptics curves.

becoming_pageturn: Horizontal paging via .scrollTargetBehavior(.paging), with the page-feel carried by .scrollTransition(.interactive) on each page's content stack — no library, no skeuomorphic curl. Three layered cues: (1) ink-settle parallax — the display element (masthead, numeral, figure) translates at ~0.92x of scroll delta while caption + folio track at 1.0x, so the page's ink appears to settle onto the paper as it lands; (2) a 2-3 degree rotation3DEffect around the leading edge on the incoming page only, decaying to zero at rest, which reads as the stiffness of a printed page rather than a sliding app tab; (3) a fore-edge shadow — during drag only, the outgoing page's trailing 24pt gains a cream→3%-cocoa vertical gradient and dims 4%, vanishing at rest so the resting page stays perfectly clean. Commit snaps on the existing Motion slow-out token with a single soft haptic detent at landfall (the her75 cascade haptic), never during the drag. Pacing is carried by the typeset folio on every page (\"PAGE THREE OF TWELVE\") instead of the deleted dashes: the book tells you where you are; no progress control does.
one_move: Delete the camera disc and make the kept sentence itself the camera — the signature interaction collapses into pure typography. This one change raises the hero to the 52pt register, removes the most app-like chrome from the highest-priority screen, turns the seal into a real seal that fills when the day is kept, and creates the struck-sentence stack that becomes the screenshot people share. It converts Home from an interface that describes the day into a page that IS the day — which is the exact distance between "beautiful health app" and "Apple Design Award finalist."
